correctness.rationale: For a one-vertex union of cycle blocks, bridge vertices can never be generated. Each outer-cycle vertex is generated exactly if its center and all remaining outer-cycle vertices are present; the center is generated exactly if one whole peripheral block is present. This proves a necessary-and-sufficient classification based on whether the center is selected and whether zero, one, or more whole blocks are selected. One partition side always has static hull, proving Radon independence; exterior vertices have a blocking deletion witness, proving Helly independence. Exhaustive direct-hull checks on 12 small graphs confirm every enumerated set and the generating polynomial, but the infinite theorem follows from the case proof.

evidence: Nair et al. investigate Helly, Radon and rank and describe characterizations for values |V|-1 and |V|-2, not the all-size independence systems for k>=3.
Aráujo et al. state polynomial-time rank algorithms for chordal and starlike graph classes; the present declared family contains an induced cycle of length at least four and is nonchordal.
The all-triangle bouquet special case is chordal and its numerical rank is not claimed as a separate contribution.
broader_coverage.reasoning: An algorithm for the numeric rank on chordal or other specified graph classes is not a theorem equating Helly, Radon and convex independence for every vertex subset on the nonchordal bouquets or giving the complete polynomial. The present maximum |V|-k for k>=3 falls strictly below the |V|-2 extremal classification. A full rank report was not inspectable and remains a priority risk.

evidence: Aráujo et al. prove the general-position number equals the maximum induced-forest size; on this family it is |V|-1.
Nair et al. focus on computational complexity and top two extremal cardinalities, whereas this theorem counts every possible cardinality of three different independence families with maximum |V|-k.
The main proof uses an exact per-cycle hub-conditioned closure classification; a generic induced-forest argument alone gives only the looser bound |V|-1.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither the rank/general-position inequality nor the known |V|-1 and |V|-2 classifications imply equality of the three independent-set systems or their generating polynomial in the nonchordal family. The known complete-multipartite coincidence does not transfer because the local cycle-completion closure rule is different.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies the entire three-system independent-set complex and all coefficients on a natural infinite, nonchordal cactus family; it also classifies every optimizer. It produces an unbounded gap k-1 between maximum induced-forest/general-position size and all three cycle-convexity invariants, precisely motivated by the recently studied distinction between these quantities. These are nontrivial structural and enumerative facts, not isolated small numerical calculations.
